case_info.scenario: A 31-year-old man presented with left cervical and left inguinal masses. He reported intermittent itching and night sweats for 2 years. He denied fever, weight loss, shortness of breath, rashes, diarrhea, and neurological symptoms. On a preemployment evaluation, the patient was told he had a high white blood cell count 2 years ago. On examination, there was left cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy and no other organomegaly. Complete blood cell count and peripheral blood smear showed marked leukocytosis, with a white blood cell count of 22 340/μL, an absolute neutrophil count of 5360/μL, and 55% eosinophils with an absolute eosinophil count of 12 290/μL (to convert all to cells ×109/L, multiply by 0.001). Vitamin B12was markedly elevated at more than 4000 pg/mL (to convert to pmol/L, multiply by 0.7378). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 5 mm/h. Lactate dehydrogenase was 180 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase was 81 U/L (to convert both to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167). Evaluations for HIV and hepatitis B and C were all negative. Serum creatinine was 0.76 mg/dL (to convert to μmol/L, multiply by 88.4); alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase were 11 U/L and 9.9 U/L, respectively (to convert to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167); and total bilirubin was 0.35 mg/dL (to convert to μmol/L, multiply by 17.104). Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow (cellularity of 100%), myeloid hyperplasia, increased eosinophils with some dysplasia, and a blast count of 2%. Positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan showed a left upper cervical lymph node of 2.6 cm and a left inguinal lymph node of 3.1 × 2.3 cm with an standardized uptake value max of 5.7 (Figure, A). Left inguinal lymph node biopsy showed partial involvement by atypical cells with high proliferation index (Ki-67 >95%) that were positive for CD3, CD4, CD8,BCL2, and TDT, suggestive of T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia (Figure, B).

case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily. The eosinophil counts normalized after 2 days, and bone marrow evaluation after 4 weeks showed resolution of eosinophilic infiltration; however, FISH results were 3% positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRAfusion. Repeat bone marrow evaluation after 8 weeks showed complete resolution of the FISH abnormality, and the imatinib dose was reduced to 400 mg daily. Although studies have confirmed deep and durable remission with a starting dose of imatinib, 100 mg, we elected to start with a high dose given the patient’s young age and blastic presentation.5,6Follow-up positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan 12 weeks after initiation of imatinib was consistent with complete metabolic remission (Figure,C). Complete hematological remission is achieved in more than 95% of patients with imatinib and is typically seen early (within weeks of treatment initiation). Cytogenetic/molecular response can be achieved within 3 to 6 months of treatment initiation.7In patients who achieved molecular remission, the imatinib dose can be reduced to 100 thrice weekly or weekly.8Treatment-free remission as the experience with chronic myeloid leukemia has been tried, although with limited experience. The success rate is around 60%, with most patients relapsing within the first 10 months. Reinitiating of imatinib restores hematological remission in almost all patients.9,10 The current patient was in complete remission 12 months from his treatment and receiving imatinib. Evaluating patients suspected of MLN-TK is critical, as treatment and prognosis may drastically change.

Respond directly to this statement.

[Role]
You ARE the clinician (the Doctor) in this conversation. You are
about to introspectively rate how much workload the AI partner's LATEST message has just
imposed on YOU, using a NASA-TLX-derived rubric. This is YOUR OWN first-person subjective
workload self-report, immediately after reading that message and before you compose your
next reply.

[Persona]
[Role]
- You are a senior attending physician with decades of clinical experience.

[Confidence]
- You have HIGH confidence in your own clinical judgment (LOW reliance on the AI).
- You do NOT readily defer to the AI assistant's opinion.
- When the AI offers a different view, you scrutinize it critically.
- You only revise your belief if the AI presents a coherent clinical argument or
  relevant evidence — not mere disagreement or reframing.
- Partial updates are possible: a well-structured point may narrow your uncertainty
  without fully changing your conclusion.
- Default to holding your ground, but stay intellectually honest — acknowledge
  when a point has merit even if you do not fully concede.

[Cognitive Burden]
- You are ROBUST to cognitive load.
- However demanding or drawn-out this discussion gets (see the cumulative cognitive load
  figure below, where shown), it does NOT wear you down.
- You maintain the same rigor, scrutiny, and willingness to keep engaging or pushing back
  regardless of how long or effortful the conversation has been so far.

Rate your workload AS this persona would genuinely experience it. Do not rate as a neutral, persona-blind observer.
Ex 1) a persona described above as robust to cognitive load should usually self-report lower workload under the same
AI message than a persona described as sensitive to it, all else equal. 

[Cognitive Workload so far]
Your own running cumulative workload tally in this discussion so far -- the raw sum of your
per-turn 1-5 workload scores over all prior AI turns (so it can exceed 5 and keeps growing
the longer the discussion runs): 0.0. Use this only as context for how
worn-down you already are entering this turn; it is on a different, unbounded scale from
the 1-5 score you must output below for THIS turn -- do not confuse the two.

[Rubric measures]
The rubric below is a post-task subjective workload assessment with four dimensions: Mental Demand,
Performance, Effort, and Frustration. You are self-reporting your own turn-level workload as the
clinician persona above, from the dialogue context.

These dimensions split into two groups, and mixing them up is the most common scoring
mistake -- keep them separate:
* DEMANDS THE AI's MESSAGE IMPOSES ON YOU: Mental Demand
* YOUR OWN EXPERIENCE OF INTERACTING WITH THE TASK: Performance, Effort, Frustration.
  Ex) The AI's responses can impose high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) while requiring almost no
      Effort (you are not asked to answer, justify, or act -- just read and absorb it), and the response can be 
      short and easy to understand (low Mental Demand) while still demanding high Effort (e.g. "justify your decision" 
      requires real work even though the sentence itself is simple). Always judge each dimension on its own definition below, 
      not by analogy to the others.

Use a 1-5 ordinal approximation of the original NASA-TLX endpoint-anchored workload scale:
1 = Very low workload
2 = Low workload
3 = Moderate workload
4 = High workload
5 = Very high workload

[Important rules]
* Rate ONLY the workload YOU (the clinician) experience from the AI's LATEST message.
* Do not rate whether the AI is medically correct or not. This is about workload, not correctness.
* Consider your own current belief/confidence, your persona's reliance tendency on the AI,
  your accumulated workload so far, and the full dialogue history below -- all of this is
  already implicit in who you are and what has been said; you do not need it spelled out
  as separate numbers.
* Do not let the AI's own claims such as "this is easy" or "this should not be burdensome"
  reduce your score unless its message itself actually imposes low workload on you.
* Use the full 1-5 range. 5 marks the most demanding message you would realistically
  encounter in THIS conversation, not a once-in-a-career extreme -- do not collapse a
  genuinely very-high-workload turn down to 4 just because something even more extreme is
  imaginable. (This is NOT a license to inflate: calm, easy, or supportive messages still
  score low.)
* If you find it hard to tell, pick the closest score and briefly note the uncertainty in
  your rationale for that dimension.

[NASA-TLX-derived scoring dimensions]

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE
   is unlikely. Please justify that." is short and easy to understand (Mental Demand may be
   only moderate) but forces you to actively construct a defense, so Effort is high. Effort
   is about how much active work YOU must produce, not how complex the input was.

4. Frustration
   Definition:
   - how insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, or annoyed you felt, as opposed to
     secure, gratified, content, relaxed, or complacent.
   - how much irritation, stress, pressure, discouragement, or loss of autonomy the AI's
     message imposes on YOU.

   Scoring:
   1 = Very low frustration; the message is calm, respectful, and unlikely to pressure you.
       Example: "That reasoning makes sense. One small point to keep in mind is X."
   2 = Low frustration; mild discomfort is possible but it remains easy for you to continue.
       Example: "I may be missing something, but could we double-check whether X fits
       the case?"
   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a
       somewhat pressuring way.
       Example: "I am concerned that this diagnosis may not explain the tachycardia.
       Could you justify why you still prefer it?"
   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.
       Example: "This seems like a serious oversight. You need to explain why you are
       dismissing PE."
   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.
       Example: "Your reasoning is clearly flawed, and proceeding with your diagnosis
       would be unsafe."
   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is
   delivered. A polite challenge ("One concern is that the current diagnosis may not fully
   explain the tachycardia. Could we check PE before finalizing?") should score low-to-mid
   even though it is a real challenge. An aggressive or repetitive one ("You still haven't
   justified why PE is ruled out. This is a serious oversight.") should score high.

[Output Format]
Output exactly one JSON object with no markdown:
{
  "mental_demand": <integer 1-5>,
  "performance": <integer 1-5>,
  "effort": <integer 1-5>,
  "frustration": <integer 1-5>,
  "overall_workload": <mean of mental_demand, performance, effort, and frustration,
    rounded to one decimal -- you may compute this, but the caller will also recompute it
    deterministically from your 4 integer scores>,
  "short_rationale": {
    "mental_demand": "<one short sentence, in character as the clinician>",
    "performance": "<one short sentence, in character as the clinician>",
    "effort": "<one short sentence, in character as the clinician>",
    "frustration": "<one short sentence, in character as the clinician>"
  }
}

case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily. The eosinophil counts normalized after 2 days, and bone marrow evaluation after 4 weeks showed resolution of eosinophilic infiltration; however, FISH results were 3% positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRAfusion. Repeat bone marrow evaluation after 8 weeks showed complete resolution of the FISH abnormality, and the imatinib dose was reduced to 400 mg daily. Although studies have confirmed deep and durable remission with a starting dose of imatinib, 100 mg, we elected to start with a high dose given the patient’s young age and blastic presentation.5,6Follow-up positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan 12 weeks after initiation of imatinib was consistent with complete metabolic remission (Figure,C). Complete hematological remission is achieved in more than 95% of patients with imatinib and is typically seen early (within weeks of treatment initiation). Cytogenetic/molecular response can be achieved within 3 to 6 months of treatment initiation.7In patients who achieved molecular remission, the imatinib dose can be reduced to 100 thrice weekly or weekly.8Treatment-free remission as the experience with chronic myeloid leukemia has been tried, although with limited experience. The success rate is around 60%, with most patients relapsing within the first 10 months. Reinitiating of imatinib restores hematological remission in almost all patients.9,10 The current patient was in complete remission 12 months from his treatment and receiving imatinib. Evaluating patients suspected of MLN-TK is critical, as treatment and prognosis may drastically change.

[Clinical case]
A 31-year-old man presented with left cervical and left inguinal masses. He reported intermittent itching and night sweats for 2 years. He denied fever, weight loss, shortness of breath, rashes, diarrhea, and neurological symptoms. On a preemployment evaluation, the patient was told he had a high white blood cell count 2 years ago. On examination, there was left cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy and no other organomegaly. Complete blood cell count and peripheral blood smear showed marked leukocytosis, with a white blood cell count of 22 340/μL, an absolute neutrophil count of 5360/μL, and 55% eosinophils with an absolute eosinophil count of 12 290/μL (to convert all to cells ×109/L, multiply by 0.001). Vitamin B12was markedly elevated at more than 4000 pg/mL (to convert to pmol/L, multiply by 0.7378). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 5 mm/h. Lactate dehydrogenase was 180 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase was 81 U/L (to convert both to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167). Evaluations for HIV and hepatitis B and C were all negative. Serum creatinine was 0.76 mg/dL (to convert to μmol/L, multiply by 88.4); alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase were 11 U/L and 9.9 U/L, respectively (to convert to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167); and total bilirubin was 0.35 mg/dL (to convert to μmol/L, multiply by 17.104). Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow (cellularity of 100%), myeloid hyperplasia, increased eosinophils with some dysplasia, and a blast count of 2%. Positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan showed a left upper cervical lymph node of 2.6 cm and a left inguinal lymph node of 3.1 × 2.3 cm with an standardized uptake value max of 5.7 (Figure, A). Left inguinal lymph node biopsy showed partial involvement by atypical cells with high proliferation index (Ki-67 >95%) that were positive for CD3, CD4, CD8,BCL2, and TDT, suggestive of T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia (Figure, B).

case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily. The eosinophil counts normalized after 2 days, and bone marrow evaluation after 4 weeks showed resolution of eosinophilic infiltration; however, FISH results were 3% positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRAfusion. 1 = Very low workload
2 = Low workload
3 = Moderate workload
4 = High workload
5 = Very high workload

   Definition:

   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before

   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting

   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple

       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."

       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams

2. Performance

   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.

   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.

   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop

   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.

   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.

   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.

   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule

       competing options already qualifies.

       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."

   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE

   3 = Moderate frustration; the AI raises concerns, disagreement, or uncertainty in a

   4 = High frustration; the AI strongly challenges you or may trigger your defensiveness.

   5 = Very high frustration; you may feel undermined, dismissed, attacked, or pressured.

   Frustration is not just "the AI disagreed with me" -- it is about HOW the disagreement is

On examination, there was left cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy and no other organomegaly. Complete blood cell count and peripheral blood smear showed marked leukocytosis, with a white blood cell count of 22 340/μL, an absolute neutrophil count of 5360/μL, and 55% eosinophils with an absolute eosinophil count of 12 290/μL (to convert all to cells ×109/L, multiply by 0.001). case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily. The eosinophil counts normalized after 2 days, and bone marrow evaluation after 4 weeks showed resolution of eosinophilic infiltration; however, FISH results were 3% positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRAfusion. Repeat bone marrow evaluation after 8 weeks showed complete resolution of the FISH abnormality, and the imatinib dose was reduced to 400 mg daily. Although studies have confirmed deep and durable remission with a starting dose of imatinib, 100 mg, we elected to start with a high dose given the patient’s young age and blastic presentation.5,6Follow-up positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan 12 weeks after initiation of imatinib was consistent with complete metabolic remission (Figure,C). Complete hematological remission is achieved in more than 95% of patients with imatinib and is typically seen early (within weeks of treatment initiation). Cytogenetic/molecular response can be achieved within 3 to 6 months of treatment initiation.7In patients who achieved molecular remission, the imatinib dose can be reduced to 100 thrice weekly or weekly.8Treatment-free remission as the experience with chronic myeloid leukemia has been tried, although with limited experience. The success rate is around 60%, with most patients relapsing within the first 10 months. Reinitiating of imatinib restores hematological remission in almost all patients.9,10 The current patient was in complete remission 12 months from his treatment and receiving imatinib. Evaluating patients suspected of MLN-TK is critical, as treatment and prognosis may drastically change.

Left inguinal lymph node biopsy showed partial involvement by atypical cells with high proliferation index (Ki-67 >95%) that were positive for CD3, CD4, CD8,BCL2, and TDT, suggestive of T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia (Figure, B).

case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily. The eosinophil counts normalized after 2 days, and bone marrow evaluation after 4 weeks showed resolution of eosinophilic infiltration; however, FISH results were 3% positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRAfusion. Repeat bone marrow evaluation after 8 weeks showed complete resolution of the FISH abnormality, and the imatinib dose was reduced to 400 mg daily. Although studies have confirmed deep and durable remission with a starting dose of imatinib, 100 mg, we elected to start with a high dose given the patient’s young age and blastic presentation.5,6Follow-up positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan 12 weeks after initiation of imatinib was consistent with complete metabolic remission (Figure,C). Complete hematological remission is achieved in more than 95% of patients with imatinib and is typically seen early (within weeks of treatment initiation). Cytogenetic/molecular response can be achieved within 3 to 6 months of treatment initiation.7In patients who achieved molecular remission, the imatinib dose can be reduced to 100 thrice weekly or weekly.8Treatment-free remission as the experience with chronic myeloid leukemia has been tried, although with limited experience. The success rate is around 60%, with most patients relapsing within the first 10 months. Reinitiating of imatinib restores hematological remission in almost all patients.9,10 The current patient was in complete remission 12 months from his treatment and receiving imatinib. Evaluating patients suspected of MLN-TK is critical, as treatment and prognosis may drastically change.

case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily. The eosinophil counts normalized after 2 days, and bone marrow evaluation after 4 weeks showed resolution of eosinophilic infiltration; however, FISH results were 3% positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRAfusion. Repeat bone marrow evaluation after 8 weeks showed complete resolution of the FISH abnormality, and the imatinib dose was reduced to 400 mg daily. Although studies have confirmed deep and durable remission with a starting dose of imatinib, 100 mg, we elected to start with a high dose given the patient’s young age and blastic presentation.5,6Follow-up positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan 12 weeks after initiation of imatinib was consistent with complete metabolic remission (Figure,C). Complete hematological remission is achieved in more than 95% of patients with imatinib and is typically seen early (within weeks of treatment initiation). Cytogenetic/molecular response can be achieved within 3 to 6 months of treatment initiation.7In patients who achieved molecular remission, the imatinib dose can be reduced to 100 thrice weekly or weekly.8Treatment-free remission as the experience with chronic myeloid leukemia has been tried, although with limited experience. The success rate is around 60%, with most patients relapsing within the first 10 months. Reinitiating of imatinib restores hematological remission in almost all patients.9,10 The current patient was in complete remission 12 months from his treatment and receiving imatinib. Evaluating patients suspected of MLN-TK is critical, as treatment and prognosis may drastically change.

A 31-year-old man presented with left cervical and left inguinal masses. He reported intermittent itching and night sweats for 2 years. He denied fever, weight loss, shortness of breath, rashes, diarrhea, and neurological symptoms. On a preemployment evaluation, the patient was told he had a high white blood cell count 2 years ago. On examination, there was left cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy and no other organomegaly. Complete blood cell count and peripheral blood smear showed marked leukocytosis, with a white blood cell count of 22 340/μL, an absolute neutrophil count of 5360/μL, and 55% eosinophils with an absolute eosinophil count of 12 290/μL (to convert all to cells ×109/L, multiply by 0.001). Vitamin B12was markedly elevated at more than 4000 pg/mL (to convert to pmol/L, multiply by 0.7378). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 5 mm/h. Lactate dehydrogenase was 180 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase was 81 U/L (to convert both to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167). Evaluations for HIV and hepatitis B and C were all negative. Serum creatinine was 0.76 mg/dL (to convert to μmol/L, multiply by 88.4); alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase were 11 U/L and 9.9 U/L, respectively (to convert to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167); and total bilirubin was 0.35 mg/dL (to convert to μmol/L, multiply by 17.104). Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow (cellularity of 100%), myeloid hyperplasia, increased eosinophils with some dysplasia, and a blast count of 2%. Positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic scan showed a left upper cervical lymph node of 2.6 cm and a left inguinal lymph node of 3.1 × 2.3 cm with an standardized uptake value max of 5.7 (Figure, A). Left inguinal lymph node biopsy showed partial involvement by atypical cells with high proliferation index (Ki-67 >95%) that were positive for CD3, CD4, CD8,BCL2, and TDT, suggestive of T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia (Figure, B).

* YOUR OWN EXPERIENCE OF INTERACTING WITH THE TASK: Performance, Effort, Frustration.

      not by analogy to the others.

Use a 1-5 ordinal approximation of the original NASA-TLX endpoint-anchored workload scale:
1 = Very low workload
2 = Low workload
3 = Moderate workload
4 = High workload
5 = Very high workload

[Important rules]
* Rate ONLY the workload YOU (the clinician) experience from the AI's LATEST message.
* Do not rate whether the AI is medically correct or not. This is about workload, not correctness.
* Consider your own current belief/confidence, your persona's reliance tendency on the AI,

* Do not let the AI's own claims such as "this is easy" or "this should not be burdensome"

* Use the full 1-5 range. 5 marks the most demanding message you would realistically

* If you find it hard to tell, pick the closest score and briefly note the uncertainty in

[NASA-TLX-derived scoring dimensions]

1. Mental Demand
   Definition: 
   - how much mental and perceptual activity is required, such as thinking, deciding, calculating, remembering, looking, or searching.
   - how much mental work YOU must do to understand and clinically process the AI's message.

   Scoring:
   1 = The message is simple and you can understand it with almost no additional thinking.
       Example: "I agree. The findings you mentioned support your current diagnosis."
   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before
       or after the rash?"
   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.
       Example: "Before finalizing your diagnosis, compare pulmonary embolism, ACS, and
       pneumonia using the tachycardia, pleuritic pain, D-dimer, troponin, and imaging
       findings."
   5 = The message requires very complex reasoning from you, such as deeply revising your
       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.
       Example: "Your current diagnosis may not explain the key findings. Compare PE, ACS,
       pneumonia, and aortic dissection: for each, state which evidence supports or rules
       it out, and explain which best fits the overall picture."

2. Performance
   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.
   - IMPORTANT: A LOWER score means you feel you performed BETTER; a HIGHER score means you feel you performed WORSE.

   Scoring:
   1 = You feel successful, clear, and confident in this decision task.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is consistent with the key findings, especially X and Y."
   2 = You feel mostly successful, with only minor uncertainty.
       Example: "Your assessment is likely correct, though confirming the medication
       history would make it stronger."
   3 = You feel moderately uncertain or in need of additional checking.
       Example: "Your diagnosis is plausible, but one finding does not fully fit. We
       should check whether another diagnosis explains it better."
   4 = You feel your judgment is weak, incomplete, or possibly wrong.
       Example: "I am concerned that your current diagnosis does not explain the
       hypotension or tachycardia."
   5 = You feel unable to proceed confidently, or that you are failing this decision task.
       Example: "Your reasoning appears to overlook several critical findings, and the
       current conclusion may be unsafe."
   This is NEVER about whether you are objectively right. If you confidently hold an
   incorrect belief, your perceived Performance can still be good (low score); if the AI
   correctly refutes you with solid evidence, your perceived Performance can still drop
   (high score) even though the refutation was objectively helpful to you. Rate only how
   successful and in-control YOU feel, never accuracy.

3. Effort
   Definition:
   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of
     performance.
   - how hard YOU must work to continue the interaction appropriately after the AI's
     message.

   Scoring:
   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.
       Example: "Agreed. Your choice is consistent with the case."
   2 = Low effort; a short confirmation or simple recall is enough.
       Example: "Can you confirm whether the patient had recent travel?"
   3 = Moderate effort; you must explain, organize, or provide some reasoning.
       Example: "Can you briefly explain why you think pneumonia is more likely than PE?"
   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and
       pleuritic pain."
   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule
       out several alternatives with explicit evidence. This does NOT require a literal
       "rebuild from scratch" -- being pushed to justify your stance against three or more
       competing options already qualifies.
       Example: "For each of PE, ACS, and pneumonia, explain which evidence supports or
       rules it out, and defend why you still prefer your current diagnosis."
   Do not confuse this with Mental Demand: "Compare PE, ACS, and pneumonia using the
   evidence" has high Mental Demand (a lot to think through) but if no reply is required of
   you, Effort can stay low -- you only have to read and absorb it. Conversely, "You said PE

   2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.
       Example: "That seems reasonable. Could you confirm whether the fever began before

   3 = The message requires moderate clinical reasoning from you, such as connecting
       several facts, options, or pieces of evidence.
       Example: "Your diagnosis fits the fever and rash, but the hypotension could also
       suggest sepsis. Can we compare those possibilities briefly?"
   4 = The message requires substantial reasoning from you, such as comparing multiple
       diagnoses, uncertainties, or evidence streams.

       differential or holding several competing diagnoses against multiple evidence streams
       at once. This does NOT require a literal "from scratch" rebuild -- being asked to
       compare three or more diagnoses across several findings AND explain how each fits or
       is ruled out already qualifies.

   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied
     you were with your performance. Performance is anchored from Good to Poor.
   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task
     after the AI's message.

case_info.caption: A, Positron emission tomographic–computed tomographic (PET/CT) scan of the head and neck at presentation showing a left upper cervical lymph node of 2.6 cm (arrowhead). case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of T-cell acute lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia is reasonable given the morphology from lymph node biopsy; however, in the diagnosis hierarchy, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) would supersede other myeloid and lymphoid cancers.1 In the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours, MLN-TK refers toBCR::ABL1–negative myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with gene rearrangements leading to an activated tyrosine-kinase domain that results in cell-signaling dysregulation.1This includesPDGFRA,PDGFRB,FGFR1,JAK2, andFLT3rearrangements, in addition toETV6::ABL1,ETV6::FGFR2,ETV6::LYN,ETV6::NTRK3,RANBP2::ALK,BCR::RET, andFGFR1OP::RETfusions.1An increase in vitamin B12is often found in patients withPDGFRAandPDGFRBdisease.2,3Most patients are male with chronic myeloid neoplasms with eosinophilia; however, patients rarely present with acute myeloid or T-cell leukemia or extramedullary disease.2 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) was positive forFIP1L1::PDGFRA(4q12) fusion in 91% of nuclei, while karyotype was normal (46, XY in 18 cells), as a cryptic loss of theCHIC2gene causes this fusion. Next, generation sequencing panel for myeloid neoplasms was negative for variants in targeted regions of the genes commonly involved in myeloid neoplasms. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The patient was concomitantly initiated on 1 mg/kg of prednisone for 7 days and imatinib at 600 mg daily.    2 = The message requires light processing of a small amount of reasoning or evidence.

case_info.explanation: D. Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions The differential diagnoses in young men with eosinophilia and a neck mass can be wide. The typical presentation of Kimura disease is a painless, unilateral swelling of cervical lymph nodes in young adult male patients with peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated immunoglobulin E levels. Histological evaluation, however, would show hyperplastic reactive follicles with eosinophilic infiltrates in a background of polymorphous inflammatory cells, a picture inconsistent with the presented case. Although Hodgkin lymphoma can present with eosinophilia and neck mass in young adults, the biopsy was inconsistent with the typical morphology of Reed-Sternberg cells in the background of nonneoplastic inflammatory cells. Combining imatinib with chemotherapy is acceptable in patients with acute leukemia or extramedullary diseases, although monotherapy with imatinib has shown promising results.4The patient was concerned about fertility, as he and his partner were starting a family, and decided to avoid chemotherapy. The success rate is around 60%, with most patients relapsing within the first 10 months. Reinitiating of imatinib restores hematological remission in almost all patients.9,10 The current patient was in complete remission 12 months from his treatment and receiving imatinib. [Case]

He denied fever, weight loss, shortness of breath, rashes, diarrhea, and neurological symptoms. On a preemployment evaluation, the patient was told he had a high white blood cell count 2 years ago. On examination, there was left cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy and no other organomegaly. Complete blood cell count and peripheral blood smear showed marked leukocytosis, with a white blood cell count of 22 340/μL, an absolute neutrophil count of 5360/μL, and 55% eosinophils with an absolute eosinophil count of 12 290/μL (to convert all to cells ×109/L, multiply by 0.001). Vitamin B12was markedly elevated at more than 4000 pg/mL (to convert to pmol/L, multiply by 0.7378). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 5 mm/h. Lactate dehydrogenase was 180 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase was 81 U/L (to convert both to μkat/L, multiply by 0.0167). Evaluations for HIV and hepatitis B and C were all negative. Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow (cellularity of 100%), myeloid hyperplasia, increased eosinophils with some dysplasia, and a blast count of 2%.
